[operator-attested] REAL TWO-PROVIDER GATE RUN — per-pass model ids, cited from the run's usage log.

COMMAND (run in worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam at HEAD 18ecd9709):
    REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=<tmp>/twoprov.toml rebar review-plan 3768-789c-11ed-48be --ref HEAD

CONFIG — two providers, set via the REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE pointer that story cb6f added, so the
checkout's own config was never edited:
    [llm.model_classes]
    frontier = { model = "anthropic:claude-opus-4-8" }
    standard = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }
    trivial  = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0" }
Resolution verified BEFORE the run via load_class_slots()/resolve_class(): frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, standard -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, trivial -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0; distinct providers = {anthropic, bedrock}.

PER-PASS MODEL IDS ACTUALLY USED — extracted from the 42 per-call `rebar.llm.structured_run` usage-log lines (each carries `model=` and `input_tokens=`):
    41 calls  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8                  96,055 input tokens
     1 call   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6       2,857 input tokens
THAT 41/1 SPLIT IS THE DECISIVE RESULT. It is EXACTLY the split this epic's consumer ticket 3768 documents for the Anthropic-only path — "41 calls on anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 (Pass-1, which escalates up from the YAML model_ladder) and 1 on anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 (the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier downgrade)" — but here the Pass-1 calls went to ANTHROPIC while the verifier downgrade dispatched to BEDROCK. So the per-pass class split survives crossing a provider boundary, which is the capability this epic exists to deliver and which no single-scalar REBAR_LLM_MODEL could express.

VERDICT PROVENANCE (the `provider_provenance` field story 343b added):
    {"provider": "bedrock", "model": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", "endpoint_host": null, "tier": "first_class", "capabilities": {"native_structured_output": false, "prompt_cache_style": "bedrock", "supports_thinking": true, "supports_temperature": true}}
Note `prompt_cache_style` resolved to "bedrock", not "anthropic" — the provider-specific capability record is live, not defaulted.

TWO HONEST QUALIFICATIONS, so this attestation is not read as stronger than it is:
1. Only ONE call exercised Bedrock, because the plan-review shape itself makes one verifier call. It proves the standard class dispatches to Bedrock end-to-end; it is NOT a load or stability test.
2. A first pass of this analysis mis-counted 4 Bedrock calls by grepping the whole log for `bedrock:<model>`; three of those matches were verdict-JSON fields, not calls. The precise count comes from lines carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`, which is 1. Corrected before writing this.

TWO REAL FINDINGS worth carrying to S6 (0d76, the Bedrock parity bar) and S9 (8625, docs):
* **Bedrock REFUSES the plain model id on-demand.** `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` fails with ValidationException: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile." The `us.`-prefixed INFERENCE PROFILE id `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` works. Verified independently with an 8-token `aws bedrock-runtime converse` before the gate run. Any Bedrock example config that omits the `us.` prefix is broken on arrival — docs/llm-example-configs.md already uses inference-profile ids.
* **Prompt caching had NO effect on the Bedrock call** (`cache_read=0, cache_write=0` at input_tokens=2857) and rebar logged a warning saying so. Worth knowing before assuming cache economics carry across providers.

Environment: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set; AWS identity arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier; Bedrock region us-east-1.
